entries.graph-theory-misc/theories/conjectures/X: The existential after the graph quantifier is the path p of C, which by its nature depends on G, C and M. The uniform quantity, the bound b on its length, is quantified before the graph (forall ell, 5 <= ell -> exists b, forall G c M ...), which is the source's 'path of C of bounded length' (arXiv:1904.12273 l.146-149) with b depending only on ell. Reviewed with wave X232 (verifier Arthur, A6 reviewer Lancelot).
entries.extremal-graph-theory/theories/conjectur: The existential after the graph quantifier is the cover P of V(G) by eps-restricted sets, which depends on G by nature. The uniform quantity, the number N of sets, is quantified before the graph (forall H a b, exists N, forall G ...), as in the source (arXiv:2105.07370 l.126-127). Part of wave X233 (verifier Arthur).

The existential after the graph quantifier is the eps-restricted set S of the conclusion, which depends on G by nature. The uniform exponent d is quantified before eps and G (forall H, exists d, forall eps G ...), as in Conjecture 1.8 of arXiv:2307.06455 (l.522-526). Part of wave X233 (verifier Arthur).

The existentials after the graph quantifier are the blocks i, j and the pure pair X, Y of the conclusion, which depend on G and the blockade by nature. The uniform constants c = 1/q and eps = 1/p are quantified before the graph (exists p q, forall G B ...), as in Question 1.3 of arXiv:2111.00532 (l.130-135). Part of wave X233 (verifier Arthur).

The existential after the graph quantifier is the eps-homogeneous set S of the conclusion, which depends on G by nature. The uniform exponents C and d are quantified before eps and G (forall F, exists C d, forall a b G ...), as in Conjecture 10 of arXiv:2403.08303 (l.327-329). Part of wave X233 (verifier Arthur).

The row quantifies over every proper hereditary family F (arXiv:2403.08303 l.327-329), as a Prop-valued predicate with the shared GTBase.graph_classes.hereditary_class (sgraph -> Prop) and an explicit properness hypothesis. Nothing is counted over F, so no Boolean version is needed. Part of wave X233 (verifier Arthur).

The row quantifies over every hereditary degree-bounded class F (arXiv:2307.08361 l.181, l.192), as a Prop-valued predicate with the shared GTBase.graph_classes.hereditary_class and the paper's degree-bounded hypothesis. Nothing is counted over F. Part of wave X233 (verifier Arthur).
entries.chromatic-theory/theories/conjectures/X2: The existential after the graph quantifier is the subgraph H of the conclusion, which depends on G by nature. The uniform threshold k = k(x, g) is quantified before the graph (forall x g, exists k, forall G ...), as in Conjecture 4 of arXiv:1808.01605 (l.91-94). Part of wave X236 (implementer Arthur, verifier Marcol).
entries.extremal-graph-theory/theories/conjectur: The existential after the graph quantifier is the forest F of the conclusion, which depends on G by nature. The density bound m = a/b is quantified before the graph (forall a b G, ...), as m is in Conjecture 7.1 of arXiv:2402.03045 (l.930-932). Part of wave X237 (implementer Marcol, verifier Arthur).
entries.chromatic-theory/theories/conjectures/X2: The row quantifies over every hereditary class C (arXiv:2202.05557 l.141-143), as a Prop-valued predicate with the shared GTBase.graph_classes.hereditary_class and the paper's hypothesis that some f : nat -> nat bounds chi by f(tau_d) on C. Nothing is counted over C, so no Boolean version is needed (as X233's polynomial_degree_bounding_statement). Part of wave X238 (verifier Marcol).

The graph quantifier that precedes the existential is inside the hypothesis (exists f, forall G t, C G -> x238_tau G d t -> chi(G) <= f t). The concluding polynomial p is quantified before the graphs it bounds (exists p, forall G t, ...), uniform over the class, as in the question of arXiv:2202.05557 l.141-143. Part of wave X238 (verifier Marcol).
entries.extremal-graph-theory/theories/conjectur: The rule matches the graph G of the conclusion, which is bound by exists, not by forall: no graph is universally quantified before an existential. The witness G and its constants c and n0 depend only on the exponent p/q, and the extremal number is required to exist for every large n, as in Erdos Problems #571. Part of wave X239 (verifier Arthur).

The existential after the graph quantifier is the vertex set S of the conclusion, which depends on G by nature. The threshold n0 is quantified before the graph (forall M, exists n0, forall G ...), as F(n) in Erdos Problems #82. Part of wave X239 (verifier Arthur).

The existential after the graph quantifier is the independent set S of the conclusion, which depends on G by nature. The constants c and n0 are quantified before the graph (forall q, exists c n0, forall G ...) and depend on delta = 1/q only, as in Erdos Problems #579. Part of wave X241 (verifier Arthur).

The existential after the graph quantifier is the k-regular subgraph H of the conclusion, which depends on G by nature. The threshold n0 is quantified before the graph (forall k q, exists n0, forall G ...) and depends on k and q only, as in Erdos Problems #182. Part of wave X242 (verifier Arthur).

The existential after the graph quantifier is the triangle-free vertex set S of the conclusion, which depends on G by nature. The constants c and n0 are quantified before the graph (forall q, exists c n0, forall G ...) and depend on delta = 1/q only, as in Erdos Problems #533. Part of wave X242 (verifier Arthur).

The existential after the graph quantifier is the C_4-free edge set F of the conclusion, which depends on G by nature. The constant c is quantified before the graph (exists c, forall G ...), an absolute constant as in Erdos Problems #1008. Part of wave X242 (verifier Arthur).

The existential after the graph quantifier is the vertex set S of the conclusion (its induced subgraph has exactly m edges), which depends on G and m by nature. The constant p (delta = 1/p) is quantified before the graph (forall C, exists p, forall G m ...) and depends on C only, as in Erdos Problems #88. Part of wave X243 (verifier Arthur).

The existential after the graph quantifier is the vertex set S of the conclusion (its induced subgraph has many distinct degrees), which depends on G by nature. The constant p is quantified before the graph (forall C, exists p, forall G ...) and depends on C only, as in Erdos Problems #637. Part of wave X243 (verifier Arthur).

The existential after the graph quantifier is the vertex v of large degree in the conclusion, which depends on G by nature. The threshold n0 is quantified before the graph (forall c, exists n0, forall G ...) and depends on c only, as in Erdos Problems #133. Part of wave X243 (verifier Arthur).

The existentials after the graph quantifier are the triangle a, b, c and the vertex set Y of the conclusion, which depend on G by nature. The threshold n0 is quantified before the graph (forall q, exists n0, forall G ...) and depends on q only, as in Erdos Problems #1034. Part of wave X243 (verifier Arthur).

The existential after the graph quantifier is the set X of added pairs in the conclusion, which depends on G by nature. The threshold n0 is quantified before the graph (forall q p, exists n0, forall G ...) and depends on q and p only, as in Erdos Problems #134. Part of wave X244 (verifier Arthur).

The existential after the graph quantifier is the set X of added pairs in the conclusion, which depends on G by nature. The constants r and n0 are quantified before the graph (forall p, exists r n0, forall G ...) and depend on p only, the uniform form of Erdos Problems #618. Part of wave X244 (verifier Arthur).

The existentials after the graph quantifier are the cut side A and the integer witness X = 8b + 1 - 4m - 8K of the conclusion, which depend on G by nature. The edge count m is quantified before the graph (forall K, exists m, forall G ...) and depends on K only, as in Erdos Problems #127. Part of wave X244 (verifier Arthur).

The existentials after the graph quantifier are the colouring col inside the hypothesis (G is not Ramsey for K_3) and the independent set S of the conclusion, which depend on G by nature. The constants q, c and n0 are quantified before the graph (exists q c n0, forall G ...), absolute as in Erdos Problems #925. Part of wave X244 (verifier Arthur).

The existential after the graph quantifier is the family F of induced subgraphs in the conclusion, which depends on G by nature. The constant p is quantified before the graph (forall C, exists p, forall G ...) and depends on C only, as in Erdos Problems #1036. Part of wave X245 (verifier Arthur).
entries.digraph-theory/theories/conjectures/X248: The row quantifies over every class C of tournaments (arXiv:2310.04265 Question 3.10, l.832-834), as a Prop-valued predicate on digraphs with the paper's class guards: closed under induced subdigraphs (x248_hereditary, l.454; no shared hereditary-class predicate exists for digraphs) and made of tournaments (heroes.is_tournament), and the hypothesis that C is polynomially dic-bounded (c * t^d). Nothing is counted over C, so no Boolean version is needed (as X238's tau_bounded_hereditary_polynomial_statement). Part of wave X248 (verifier Marcol).

The row quantifies over every class C of digraphs (arXiv:2310.04265 Conjecture 6.1, l.1477-1479), as a Prop-valued predicate on digraphs with the paper's class guards: closed under induced subdigraphs (x248_hereditary, l.454) and made of oriented digraphs (heroes_dichotomy.oriented_dg; the paper's digraphs have no loops or digons, l.377), and the hypothesis that C is dic-bounded with the digraph clique number. Nothing is counted over C, so no Boolean version is needed (as X238's tau_bounded_hereditary_polynomial_statement). Part of wave X248 (verifier Marcol).
entries.extremal-graph-theory/theories/conjectur: The existential after the graph quantifier is the family Fs of copies of C_4 (4-edge sets of G) in the conclusion, which depends on G by nature. The constant c is quantified before the graph (exists c, forall G ...) and is absolute, as in Erdos Problems #60 and He, Ma and Yang, arXiv:1912.00986v1, p.3 (h(n) >= c sqrt n for some constant c > 0). Part of wave X247 (verifier Arthur).

The existentials after the graph quantifier are the vertices x, y, z of the triangle in the conclusion, which depend on G by nature. The threshold n0 is quantified before the graph (forall q, exists n0, forall G ...) and depends on q (o(1) = 1/q) only, as in Erdos Problems #1033. Part of wave X247 (verifier Arthur).
entries.digraph-theory/theories/conjectures/X251: The row quantifies over every family F of digraphs (arXiv:2410.23566 Conjecture 7, l.184-186), as a Prop-valued predicate on digraphs with the source's hypotheses: F linearly unavoidable (the library's linearly_unavoidable, relational in the unavoidability number) and of bounded maximum average degree (x251_mad_le). Nothing is counted over F, so no Boolean version is needed (as X248's two class rows and X238's tau_bounded_hereditary_polynomial_statement). Part of wave X251 (verifier Marcol).
entries.extremal-graph-theory/theories/conjectur: The existential after the graph quantifier is the constant c of ex(n;G) << n^{3/2} inside the left side of the biconditional, which depends on the fixed graph G by nature (the implied constant of ex(n;G) is G's), as in Erdos Problems #113 and Janzer's Conjecture 1.3. Part of wave X252 (verifier Arthur).

The existential after the graph quantifier is the vertex v of the conclusion, which depends on G by nature. The constant c is quantified before the graph (forall r, exists c, forall G ...) and depends on r only (d >>_r n), as in Erdos Problems #1079 and Bollobas-Thomason's c_r. Part of wave X252 (verifier Arthur).
entries.chromatic-theory/theories/conjectures/X2: The existentials after the graph quantifier are the number n of Kempe changes and the colouring col' of the conclusion (a proper member of the Kempe class of col using fewer than t colours), which depend on G and col by nature: every class must contain such a member, as in Las Vergnas and Meyniel's Conjecture A' (arXiv:2103.10684v2, l.160-162). No constant is quantified. Part of wave X256 (verifier Marcol).

The existential after the graph quantifier is the number n of Kempe changes from col1 to col2 (Kempe equivalence), which depends on G and the two colourings by nature. The constant c is quantified before the graph (exists c, forall t G ...) and is absolute, as the source's c' (arXiv:2103.10684v2, Question 1.7, l.199-201). Part of wave X256 (verifier Marcol).

The existential after the graph quantifier is the number n of Kempe changes from col1 to col2 (Kempe equivalence), which depends on G and the two colourings by nature; no constant is quantified, as in Mohar's conjecture as stated (arXiv:1503.03430v2, l.53). Part of wave X256 (verifier Marcol).

The existentials after the graph quantifier are the number n of Kempe changes and the colouring col reached from col1 that agrees with col2 on the edges (Kempe equivalence of edge colourings; values on non-adjacent pairs never move), which depend on G and the two colourings by nature; no constant is quantified, as in Mohar's conjecture (arXiv:2107.07900v1, Conjecture 1.4, l.184-186). Part of wave X256 (verifier Marcol).

The existential after the graph quantifier is the subgraph H, which depends on G by nature (each graph of chromatic number m contains its own H). The constant C is quantified before the graph (exists C, forall G m ...) and is absolute, as in Alon, Krivelevich and Sudakov's Theorem 1.1 (AKS97.txt l.29-30). Part of wave X261 (verifier Marcol).

The existential after the graph quantifier is the number k of colours of an acyclic colouring of that G, which depends on G by nature. q and the threshold on d are quantified before the graph, so q k <= d^2 bounds every graph of maximum degree d, as f(d) is the maximum over them (Alon, McDiarmid and Reed, p.278). Part of wave X261 (verifier Marcol).
entries.extremal-graph-theory/theories/conjectur: The existentials after the graph quantifier are the vertex set S and the degree d of the conclusion (G[S] d-regular and non-trivial), which depend on G by nature. The constants q and N are quantified before the graph (exists q N, forall G ...) and are absolute, the >> log n of Erdos Problems #1031. Part of wave X263 (verifier Arthur).
